market_summary: US futures are flat (S&P ~7,692) after Tuesday's gains; after hours Intuit fell 7% on a 9-10% FY27 growth guide, Zoom -3.9%, and Semtech guided Q3 revenue to $405-415M against $379M consensus. The 10-year is 4.63%, WTI $81 after Iran and Oman proposed a temporary Hormuz shipping corridor, bitcoin ~$78,600 and AUD/USD ~0.716. Asia set-up: Nikkei futures +0.2% at ~66,020, ASX 200 futures +0.3% after Tuesday's 9,165 close; Alibaba's HK$80B placement settles today and SK hynix wage talks restart from scratch. Australian July CPI lands 11:30 AEST (consensus headline 3.2-3.3% from 3.8%, trimmed mean 3.5%; RBA at 4.35% with ~13% odds of a September hike). Tonight 22:30 AEST: July PCE (core 0.2% m/m, 3.3% y/y consensus) and the Q2 GDP second estimate; then Nvidia ~6:30am AEST Thursday (consensus $92.2B revenue, $2.09 EPS, Q3 guide bar ~$104B, first Rubin shipments) alongside Salesforce, CrowdStrike and Synopsys, and Fed chair Warsh at Jackson Hole at 12am AEST Saturday.

AMZN.reason: Closed down 0.4% at $261.06 and $260.89 after hours, no overnight catalyst. New PYMNTS data puts Amazon at 17.8% of US clothing spend in 2026 (8.5% in 2019) versus Walmart's 6.0%, with $55.5B of apparel sales in H1, useful for the retail margin story but secondary to AWS. With $220B capex, Bezos selling and state antitrust suits still capping the multiple, hold.

AXOS.reason: Closed up 1.9% at $98.82, flat after hours, with nothing new after Tuesday's NYSE Texas dual-listing announcement. Benchmark's $120 target (Aug 17) and 17% ROE support continuing to hold.

BABA.reason: ADR closed up 0.8% at $119.44 ($119.52 after hours); the HK$80B placement of 710M shares at HK$112.70 is due to close today, Wednesday, so Hong Kong trading from 11:30 AEST shows whether insider buying (Ma >HK$600M, Tsai and Wu HK$202M) holds the line. HK close Tuesday was HK$114.20, only 1.3% above the placement price; wait for a base before adding.

ENPH.reason: Closed up 0.5% at $37.35 and $37.26 after hours with no new news overnight. Q3 revenue guide is $290-320M, below last year, and the Dutch net-metering campaign, AI assistant and IQ Battery C80 are incremental, so stay on the sidelines until residential demand stabilizes.

FIGR.reason: Closed up 6.5% at $41.14, giving back 0.5% to $40.94 after hours, with no follow-on news after the EDX Markets YLDS collateral integration. Q2 revenue +121% to $198.8M and marketplace volume +132% to $4.3B underpin Bernstein's $70 target; hold and let execution play out.

GOOGL.reason: Closed down 0.3% at $346.96 and $347.20 after hours. Overnight additions are small: Ask Gemini in Google Chat rolls out to Workspace customers from Aug 26 and a distributed-database vendor (Rezolv AI) was selected by Google. The bigger drivers are unchanged: Cloud +82%, Waymo's Munich launch for 2027, Morgan Stanley's ~$200B TPU cloud-revenue case, and the stock sitting ~3% under its 50-day average near $358, so the post-Jeff-Dean dip remains an entry.

LDI.reason: Closed up 3.7% at $0.92 and $0.94 after hours, still below the $1 NYSE threshold with a six-month cure window running from the Aug 21 notice. Goldman is at Sell with a $1 target; exchange-compliance and reverse-split or dilution risk argue for reducing exposure.

META.reason: Closed up 2% at $570.05, easing to $568.01 after hours. In the 29-state trial Adam Mosseri denied any policy of suppressing child-safety risks, but Instagram's product-design director Francesco Fogu conceded that data showing teens saw 1.5x more bullying, suicide, hate and violent content than adults was removed from a 2023 safety presentation, and that 'take a break' adoption would suffer without being default. Trial runs through September with penalties up to ~$200B sought; with $125-145B capex and the stock ~26% down YTD, hold pending trial clarity.

MRVL.reason: Closed up 4.8% at $240.38 and ticked to $241.52 after hours after Rosenblatt (Buy, $300), Susquehanna ($265) and Wells Fargo ($310) target moves tied to the Google warrant deal (240 tranches vesting per $500M of custom-silicon purchases, ~$120B through FY2033). Thursday's print (Fri ~6:30am AEST) faces ~$2.71B revenue and $0.93 EPS consensus, but the real bar is Q3 guidance versus the $3.03B street number; with the stock up ~160% YTD and options implying a ~12% move, hold through the report.

MU.reason: Closed up 2.5% at $932.97 ($935.00 after hours), still about 3% below the 50-day average after Monday's CXMT/YMTC-for-Apple drop; Gartner's Aug 24 update sees memory revenue at $837B in 2026 (DRAM +247%) and above $1T in 2027 with new fabs not rebalancing supply through 2027, which supports the HBM sold-out story even as Mizuho trimmed its target to $1,300 and Barron's argues long-term contracts cap Micron's share of a 50% price rise. Nvidia's print tonight is the next swing factor, so hold.

NFLX.reason: Closed up 2.8% at $82.23 ($82.16 after hours) on Wolfe's $95 target (22x 2028 EPS of $4.41) and its read that Q2's soft engagement was a scheduling issue; nothing new overnight. Still ~36% below the 52-week high with ad-tier, NFL and rival-streamer hosting optionality, so the valuation reset remains an add.

NVDA.reason: Closed up 2.2% at $213.05 and $214.17 after hours ahead of the print (Thu ~6:30am AEST). Consensus is ~$92.2B revenue (vs $91B +/-2% guide, ex-China) and ~$2.06-2.09 EPS, with the street looking for a Q3 guide near $104.2B (+83% y/y) and ~75% gross margin; Morgan Stanley pegs Rubin at nearly $9B of Q3 sales, while analysts want detail on custom-chip competition (Jalapeno, TPUs), buyback framework, memory cost pass-through and the ~$500B customer-financing exposure. Options imply a 5-6% move, the smallest into an Nvidia print in years; hold and reassess after guidance.

RKT.reason: Closed up 1.5% at $14.30, unchanged after hours, with no news since the Rowan AI-agent launch for Rocket Money's Premium Plus tier; the 10-year at 4.62% helps refi volume at the margin, but after the ~50% run and Q2's 9.6% post-earnings drop the shares look fully priced, so hold.

TSM.reason: Closed up 1.8% at $417.41 ($417.76 after hours) after Taipei shares rose 1.05% to NT$2,400 on Tuesday; Taipei had not yet opened at 08:30 AEST, and Wednesday's session will trade off Nvidia positioning before the print. No new company news overnight; with 40%+ 2026 growth guidance, Apple's 2nm M6 and up-to-10% 2027 price rises, the pullback from the June high remains a buying opportunity.

STRIPE.reason: No new valuation event: the OpenRouter acquisition (~$7B), Treasury in Australia and the Gartner billing-leader rating are steady expansion, not a mark change, so hold the private position. Marked at 2.27x cost: latest valuation ~$159B (2026-02) vs ~$70B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/24/stripes-valuation-soars-74-to-159-billion/).

OPENAI.reason: Nothing new overnight beyond the o3 retirement from ChatGPT on Aug 26; the open questions remain the four senior departures ahead of a 2027 IPO, ~$750B of planned compute spend through 2030 backed partly by Nvidia guarantees, and whether Jalapeno's per-watt benchmarks translate to 2027 volume. Nvidia's call tonight may add colour on the $105B Ohio guarantee. Private, so hold. Marked at 5.43x cost: latest valuation ~$852B (2026-08) vs ~$157B at entry (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/10/openai-reportedly-completed-a-7-billion-employee-tender-offer/).

headlines: Nvidia reports ~6:30am AEST Thursday: consensus $92.2B revenue, $2.09 EPS, Q3 guide bar ~$104B; NVDA $214.17 after hours, options imply 5-6%.
Tonight 22:30 AEST: July PCE (core 0.2% m/m consensus) and Q2 GDP revision; Australian July CPI 11:30 AEST, consensus 3.2-3.3% from 3.8%.
Watchlist: Credo (CRDO) added, FY26 revenue tripled, reports Sep 1; Spotify dropped as the slowest grower, stays on loves.
Meta trial: Instagram design chief conceded teen harmful-content data was cut from a 2023 safety deck, Mosseri denied suppression; META $568 after hours.
After hours: Intuit -7% on a 9-10% FY27 growth guide; S&P futures flat, WTI $81 as Iran and Oman float a Hormuz corridor.
TrendForce: memory to absorb 68% of hyperscaler capex in 2027, server DRAM ~+270% in 2026; Gartner sees $837B memory revenue in 2026.
